messages:
anya (prod): Quick decision needed: Do we ship 'staggered burst windows' for Dedicated commits? Idea: allow a single commit to be exposed as multiple time-sliced windows with region affinity so customers get predictable local capacity without overallocating globally. Pros: better utilization, regional SLAs. Cons: added admission logic + telemetry. Thoughts?

mike (eng-platform): Sounds promising for global customers. Main unknown: autoscale interaction. If windows are tiny and local, prewarm/pooled kernels might lose efficiency. Need a model.

joel (infra): Implementation note: we can model windows as disjoint leases on the same commit id. Each window has its own preemptable flag and affinity tag. Admission sums active tokens across windows. Prefill cache lazily when window first activates.

ravi (sre): Ops concerns: (1) fragmentation causing many small preempt events, (2) cross-region failover complexity. Must provide a way to collapse windows into a single pool for emergency.

li (data): We should track per-window KPIs: activation_rate, avg_tokens/sec, preempt_pct, and pool_spillbacks. That will let us detect pathological tenants.

anya (prod): Proposed defaults: max_windows=4, min_window_duration=15m, affinity optional (region string), spillback_policy=spill-to-shared-pool. Preempt order: LIFO across windows by activation time.

mike (eng-platform): Expose config example?

joel (infra): Quick sample config we can show in API docs:

```json
{"commit_id": "C-12345", "staggered_windows": 3, "window_duration": "30m", "min_window_tokens": 100000, "affinity": ["us-west-2"], "spillback": "shared_pool", "preempt": "LIFO"}
```

ravi (sre): Canary plan: internal canary for 10 days on low-risk reserved pool, gates: token-latency median <= SLO+10ms, 99th <= SLO+50ms, preempt_rate < 1% and no >10x increase in oncall paged incidents related to evictions.

anya (prod): Launch criteria: engineering + infra + ops signoff, zero regressions on eval suite, two pilot customers (one regional chat provider, one analytics batch workload) sign off, console shows per-window usage.

sophia (sales): I have a regional chat prospect in EMEA who will try this if we can provide region affinity and <3 minute failover window. They want a pilot timeline.

mike (eng-platform): Rough estimate: MVP (3 windows, basic affinity, console usage) = 3 sprints (6 weeks). Extra sprint for autoscale tuning and perf work.

joel (infra): Risk register: (a) bookkeeping growth if customers create many tiny windows, (b) telemetry gaps for per-window metrics, (c) increased memory usage for per-window KV prewarm state. Mitigations: cap windows per commit (4), min token threshold, and telemetry rollout.

ravi (sre): Ops playbook items: admin endpoint to merge/collapse windows; emergency flag to route all active windows to shared pooled capacity; alert when preempt rate per-window > 0.5%. I'll draft runbook.

li (data): I'll add dashboards and a daily job to surface top windows by evictions and by wasted tokens (idle but reserved).

anya (prod): Decision poll: ship MVP with defaults above and canary plan? Reply with +1.

mike (eng-platform): +1

joel (infra): +1

ravi (sre): +1 (will own ops runbook)

sophia (sales): +1 (will align pilot customer)

capacity-bot: ACTIONS: anya -> update roadmap & public spec; mike -> detailed implementation plan + cost model; joel -> infra PR + perf tests; ravi -> ops playbook + alerts; li -> dashboards; sophia -> pilot signoff. Preliminary due: 6 weeks.

anya (prod): One open question for pricing: do we discount idle hold for per-window reservations vs full-commit? Flagging pricing sync next Tue.

mike (eng-platform): I'll prepare a delta-cost model comparing pooled prewarm vs per-window prewarm.

anya (prod): Thanks everyone. Closing thread unless objections. :white_check_mark:
